chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: Avoiding imitation and singing songs straight
summary: She stayed away from another singer's style and tried to sing straight.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Well I tried to stay away from her style as much as possible.

Yeah. Because when I first came to New York I wanted to sing. I thought singing like Ella Fitzgerald was the thing to do. But it wasn't and that's how I got locked into things like "Loch Lomond" because not only was it different styling, it was a different type of repertoire and it put me in a field all by myself, so to speak, because I wasn't just doing pop music. On the records I made, although there was usually a standard pop tune on one side, the intent was to sell the folk thing.
When you approached those songs just from the point of view of vocal techniques I guess, did you try and do different things with your voice?

No, I tried to sing them straight. Of course, I like to pay attention to the lyrics and the delivery of the lyrics. If anything I concentrate on the phrasing. Try to make the lyrics not only fit the music but also to make some kind of sense instead of just
